note: Thursday 29 Oct 2026 07:02 SGT run, covering the Wednesday 28 Oct US close / pre-Thursday-Asia-open snapshot. S&P 500 +0.28% to 7743.98, Nasdaq +0.27% to 26549.85, Dow +0.19% to 52475.10, Russell 2000 +0.41% to 2830.51, VIX fell a third straight session (-3.48%) to 16.91. The FOMC decision landed 14:00 ET Wed (02:00 SGT Thu); a separate stream is covering the outcome in depth. Equity Fear & Greed: third-party trackers (CNN's own site returned 451/403 blocks again this run) converge on ~34/100 (Fear), up modestly from ~27-28 Tuesday, driven mainly by the VIX's third straight decline and steady junk-bond demand, while Safe-Haven Demand remains the weakest/most fearful component (~15, Extreme Fear). Crypto Fear & Greed eased to 51 (Neutral) from the high-50s/60s a week ago. NYSE breadth on Wednesday: wire-service recaps put advancers ahead of decliners by a ~1.05-to-1 ratio (Nasdaq advancers led 1.48-to-1), consistent with all four major indices closing higher, though one automated tracker (stockmarketwatch.com) showed an opposite negative snapshot this run that looks stale/mistimed and is flagged as lower-confidence. 52-week breadth stayed mixed: NYSE 110 new highs vs 214 new lows (net negative) even as the S&P 500 itself posted a slim net-positive 19-vs-14. %-above-200DMA/50DMA and the McClellan Oscillator/Summation Index could not be refreshed past Oct 21-23 prints this run (StockCharts/mcoscillator.com blocked automated access); those rows remain stale context, not Oct 28 prints. flows.narrative: In the week ending Oct 21, emerging-market and China equity funds drew their strongest inflows in months even as BofA's institutional clients logged their 10th-largest weekly US equity selling week since 2008. Cash and Treasuries both gathered fresh money ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting, Europe booked a second straight week of outflows, and gold kept its safe-haven bid despite miners' rough October on the tape. Re-verified Thursday 29 Oct pre-Asia-open: explicitly confirmed no newer weekly edition has been published -- the figures below are unchanged from the prior run and should NOT be read as fresh. The next BofA/EPFR print (week ended Oct 28) is due Fri Oct 30 and will be the first to capture this week's FOMC decision (held Wed 28 Oct), the Wed Oct 28 close (S&P 7743.98, VIX 16.91, a third straight VIX decline), Core PCE/GDP, the ECB/BOJ catalyst cluster, plus the Mon 26-Tue 27 Oct Anthropic-IPO-driven AI rally and Asia-wide Southbound/Korea/China-margin de-risking already visible in the investor-type data.

Hedge funds sold for the first time in 5 weeks and retail/private clients also sold (reversing the prior 2 weeks' buying), leaving BofA's total client book at a record -$14.8B single-stock net outflow, partially offset by +$2.8B of equity-ETF inflows across styles/cap segments
